holds.reason: 王叔仁 is the courtesy name of Wang Yun (s0230 王蘊，字叔仁), who asked to be sent out to a command. The local record's personal-name claim "Wang Shu" (c0047) and the s0021 English "Wang Shu" are wrong: Wang Shu (述) is a different man (s0223). Held until the name is corrected; the referent itself is attested.

editorialRepairs.before: Chu Pou shrank from wielding power at court, and Wang Shu begged to be sent to the frontier; both kept their skins and their honor, and deserve mention.
editorialRepairs.after: Chu Pou shrank from wielding power at court, and Wang Yun begged to be sent to the frontier; both kept their skins and their honor, and deserve mention.
editorialRepairs.sourceBasedReason: 王叔仁 is the courtesy name of Wang Yun (s0230 王蘊，字叔仁). "Wang Shu" wrongly names him and could be confused with Wang Shu 述 (s0223).
editorialRepairs.pairedFieldChecked: As for Chu Yeye’s fearing and avoiding court power, and Wang Shuren’s firmly seeking to go out and hold a command, by this they were able to preserve the body and keep far from harm—there is something to praise in that.
